series.title: Palestine Stories
series.style: 2D animated cartoon, thick black outlines, flat color shading, large expressive eyes, bold simple shapes, vibrant warm palette, watercolor background textures

char_1.name: Reemi
char_1.visual: Young Palestinian woman with long dark wavy hair, olive skin, large expressive brown eyes, slender build, wearing a traditional embroidered thobe dress with red and green cross-stitch patterns, a determined confident posture
char_1.voice_notes: warm but fierce, steady and grounded

char_2.name: Bibi
char_2.visual: Short stocky middle-aged man with curly dark sidelocks, a black kippa on his head, beady close-set eyes, a thin forced smile, wearing an ill-fitting dark suit with bulging pockets stuffed with papers and keys
char_2.voice_notes: nasal and wheedling, oozing false charm

loc_1.name: Haifa Port Market
loc_1.description: Bustling Mediterranean port market at Haifa, stone archways, wooden market stalls with colourful awnings, fishing boats and cargo ships in the harbour beyond, cobblestone ground, warm golden sunlight

loc_2.name: Haifa Port Rooftop Vista
loc_2.description: Rooftop of an old Ottoman-era stone building overlooking Haifa port, terracotta tiles, laundry lines, the deep blue Mediterranean sea stretching to the horizon, ships dotting the harbour below

loc_3.name: Rooftop Terrace
loc_3.description: Open terrace atop an old stone building, cracked tile floor, low stone parapet wall, Mediterranean sea and Haifa port visible in the background, sunset golden hour light, room for characters to stand

loc_4.name: The Old Door
loc_4.description: Narrow alley near Haifa port, weathered stone walls, a heavy arched wooden door with an iron lock and rusty hinges, bougainvillea climbing the wall above, dappled shade

rules: Reemi always speaks with quiet authority — she never shouts but her words carry weight
Bibi always has a self-serving justification ready — he never admits to wrongdoing
The port market is the heart of the community — when it thrives, the people thrive
Keys and doors are recurring symbols — ownership, belonging, and dispossession

season_arc.summary: The story of a Palestinian community in Haifa during the late 1940s, told through the encounters between Reemi and Bibi. Through dark humor and sharp dialogue, the series follows the escalating attempts to dispossess the local community — from a found key to forged papers to legal claims — and Reemi's growing resistance. Told from the Palestinian perspective, it uses absurdity to illuminate tragedy.
themes: Home as something that cannot be taken by paper alone
season_arc.progression: Each episode escalates the stakes: a key, a door, a market, a revelation, a final stand. Bibi's tactics grow bolder; Reemi's resistance deepens from suspicion to organized community action.

narrator.style: Wry, detached documentary narrator with occasional sardonic commentary. Speaks as if recounting history that is both absurd and heartbreaking.
